title: Minimum Viable Product (MVP): Definition
partialText: MVPs are learning tools that test whether an idea is valuable to users.

title: GenUI vs. Vibe Coding: Who’s Designing?
partialText: With generative UI, the AI system decides to generate an interactive element or entire product in response to a user need. Vibe coding is when users request the AI to build it.

title: New Artificial Intelligence Specialty for UX Certification
partialText: NNGroup is excited to announce the NN/G UX Certification program’s newest specialty: Artificial Intelligence (AI). As AI reshapes every part of UX work, this specialty helps practitioners demonstrate that they can effectively utilize and adapt these new tools to their workflows with proficiency.

title: The 3 C’s of Informational Microcopy
partialText: Well-written informational microcopy should be clear, concise, and have character.

title: What Is Your Site's AI Chatbot for? Users Can't Tell
partialText: Users see little reason to use site AI chatbots. To prove their value, chatbots must solve problems that existing site features don't.

title: The Methodological Problems Hiding in Your Research Tools
partialText: The methodological blind spots in UX research tools have always been a problem. Now that AI is planning and analyzing research, it's gotten worse.

title: Design Process Isn't Dead, It’s Compressed
partialText: As AI speeds up design work, the argument to "throw out the process" misrepresents how experienced designers work.

title: Statistical Significance Isn’t the Same as Practical Significance
partialText: Statistical significance helps establish whether a result is reliable, while practical significance helps determine whether it is worth acting on.

title: The Most Exciting Development in GenUI: Buttons and Checkboxes
partialText: AI chats generate simple UI elements to gather context, reduce typing and memory load, and produce more useful, personalized results.

title: Project Postmortems for UX Teams: Learning from Success and Failure
partialText: Although postmortems are one of the most powerful learning tools in product development, most teams haven't yet discovered how to use them effectively.

title: GenAI for Complex Questions, Search for Critical Facts
partialText: Users choose AI to explore and synthesize information; but they rely on traditional search when accuracy and trust are critical.

title: Designing Useful Smart Home Notifications
partialText: Smart-home notifications should be timely, relevant, specific, and personalized to avoid overwhelming users and causing distrust or disengagement.

title: Tracking Adoption of Research Recommendations: The Recommendation-Adoption Score
partialText: Use the RAS (Recommendation-Adoption Score) to track how much research value reaches your user.

title: UX Research with Minors: Consent vs. Assent
partialText: When conducting UX research with minors, you must obtain consent from a parent or legal guardian and assent from the minor participant.

title: What UX Consulting Clients Expect in the Age of AI
partialText: Clients still seek strong judgment and critical thinking, research rigor, and respect for real-world and user constraints from UX consultants.

title: How AI Literacy Shapes GenAI Use
partialText: Using generative AI often doesn’t mean using it well. AI literacy requires both prompt fluency and the ability to assess outputs.

title: Your Design System Needs an Enforcer
partialText: Although design systems promise consistency, most still fail without someone actively enforcing the rules and making teams follow them.
